definition: A compound that, on administration, undergoes conversion by biochemical (enzymatic), chemical (possibly following an enzymatic step), or physical (e.g. photochemical) activation processes before becoming the active agent for which it is a pro-agent.
label: pro-agent

definition: An amino disaccharide consisting of an α-<small>D</small>-glucopyranose residue and a 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-<small>D</small>-glucopyranose residue joined in sequence by a (1→6) glycosidic bond.
label: alpha-D-Glcp-(1->6)-D-GlcpNAc

definition: Any compound that is able to prevent damage to the kidneys.
label: renoprotective agent

definition: A food preservative which prevents decomposition of food by preventing the growth of fungi or bacteria. In European countries, E-numbers for permitted food preservatives are from E200 to E299, divided into sorbates (E200-209), benzoates (E210-219), sulfites (E220-229), phenols and formates (E230-239), nitrates (E240-259), acetates (E260-269), lactates (E270-279), propionates (E280-289) and others (E290-299).
label: antimicrobial food preservative

definition: An organic cation obtained by protonation of the  six amino groups of framycetin; major species at pH 7.3.
label: framycetin(6+)

definition: Any compound that inhibits the biosynthesis of any sterol.
label: sterol biosynthesis inhibitor

definition: A broad-spectrum highly toxic antibiotic or mixture of antibiotics produced by a streptomyces (Streptomyces fradiae) and used medically especially to treat local infections.
label: neomycin

definition: Any six-carbon monosaccharide which in its linear form contains either an aldehyde group at position 1 (aldohexose) or a ketone group at position 2 (ketohexose).
label: hexose

definition: Intended use of the molecular entity or part thereof by humans.
label: application

definition: Salts and esters of sulfuric acid
label: sulfates

definition: A substance used to lower plasma cholesterol levels.
label: anticholesteremic drug

definition: A 2-amino-2-deoxy-<small>D</small>-glucopyranose with an α-configuration at the anomeric position.
label: alpha-D-glucosamine

definition: A proteinogenic amino acid derivative resulting from reaction of <small>L</small>-methionine  at the amino group or the carboxy group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen of <small>L</small>-methionine by a heteroatom.
label: L-methionine derivative

definition: An organic triphosphate formed by condensation between the γ-phospho group of guanosine 5'-triphosphate and ethanol.
label: ethyl-GTP

definition: A hemiacetal having the structure RR<small><sup>1</small></sup>C(OH)OR<small><sup>2</small></sup> (R, R<small><sup>1</small></sup>, R<small><sup>2</small></sup> ≠ H), derived from a ketone by formal addition of an alcohol to the carbonyl group.
label: hemiketal

definition: A compound in which a carbonyl group is bonded to two carbon atoms: R<small><sub>2</sub></small>C=O (neither R may be H).
label: ketone

definition: A macrocyclic lactone with a ring of twelve or more members derived from a polyketide.
label: macrolide

definition: Antidepressants are mood-stimulating drugs used primarily in the treatment of affective disorders and related conditions.
label: antidepressant

definition: A primary diamine is a compound derived from a hydrocarbon by replacing two hydrogen atoms by amino groups.
label: primary diamine

definition: A drug used to prevent nausea or vomiting. An antiemetic may act by a wide range of mechanisms: it might affect the medullary control centres (the vomiting centre and the chemoreceptive trigger zone) or affect the peripheral receptors.
label: antiemetic

definition: Substances which are added to food in order to prevent decomposition caused by  microbial growth or by undesirable chemical changes.
label: food preservative

definition: Any substance which is used to reduce or control weight.
label: anti-obesity agent

definition: A pyranobenzodioxin and antibiotic that is active against gram-negative bacteria and used (as its dihydrochloride pentahydrate) to treat gonorrhea. It is produced by the bacterium Streptomyces spectabilis.
label: spectinomycin

definition: Any member of the class of fluorobenzenes containing a mono- or poly-substituted benzene ring carrying two fluorine atoms.
label: difluorobenzene

definition: A glycosyl alditol consisting of α-D-glucopyranose and (2ξ)-D-arabino-hexitol residues joined in sequence by a (1→1) glycosidic bond.
label: (2xi)-6-O-alpha-D-glucopyranosyl-D-arabino-hexitol

definition: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing three hydrogen atoms by organyl groups.
label: tertiary amino compound

definition: A glucosylglucose consisting of β-<small>L</small>-fucopyranose and α-<small>D</small>-glucopyranose residues joined in sequence by a (1→3) glycosidic bond.
label: beta-L-Fucp-(1->3)-alpha-D-Glcp

definition: A <small>L</small>-methionine derivative in which one of the hydrogens attached to the nitrogen is replaced by a formyl group.
label: N-formyl-L-methionine

definition: A <small>L</small>-glucopyranose with an α-configuration at the anomeric position.
label: alpha-L-glucose

definition: Any alkali metal salt having sodium(1+) as the cation.
label: sodium salt

definition: Any drug found useful in the symptomatic treatment of diarrhoea.
label: antidiarrhoeal drug

definition: A mixture of cyclic polypeptide streptogramin antibiotics produced by Streptomyces virginiae, S. loidensis, S. mitakaensis, S. pristina-spiralis, S. ostreogriseus, and others. The two major components are virginiamycin M1 (also known as pristinamycin IIA) and virginiamycin S1. Virginiamycin has been widely used as a growth promotion agent in livestock and has been to have bacteriostatic activity against Gram-positive organisms such as staphylococci and streptococci.
label: virginiamycin

definition: Any eukaryotic metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in algae including unicellular organisms like chlorella and diatoms to multicellular organisms like giant kelps and brown algae.
label: algal metabolite

definition: A drug that affects the rate or intensity of cardiac contraction, blood vessel diameter or blood volume.
label: cardiovascular drug

definition: Organic compounds containing an oxygen atom, =O, doubly bonded to carbon or another element.
label: organic oxo compound

definition: A drug used to treat or prevent bacterial infections.
label: antibacterial drug

definition: A molecular entity that contains no carbon.
label: inorganic molecular entity

definition: A fused-ring β-lactam system where the β-lactam ring is fused to a 1,3-oxazolidine ring.
label: oxapenam

definition: A trideoxyhexose derivative that is α-<small>D</small>-glucose in which the 2 and 6-hydroxy groups are replaced by amino groups while the 3-hydroxy group is replaced by hydrogen.
label: 2,6-diamino-2,3,6-trideoxy-alpha-D-glucose

definition: A biomacromolecule consisting of large numbers of monosaccharide residues linked glycosidically. This term is commonly used only for those containing more than ten monosaccharide residues.
label: polysaccharide

definition: A substance used to treat hyperlipidemia (an excess of lipids in the blood).
label: antilipemic drug

definition: Any compound which acts on the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor.
label: PPAR modulator

definition: An EC 1.14.14.* (oxidoreductase acting on paired donors, incorporating of 1 atom of oxygen, with reduced flavin or flavoprotein as one donor) inhibitor that interferes with the action of an unspecified monooxygenase (EC 1.14.14.1).
label: EC 1.14.14.1 (unspecific monooxygenase) inhibitor

definition: A cyclic compound containing nine or more atoms as part of the cyclic system.
label: macrocycle

definition: A drug which increases appetite.
label: appetite enhancer

definition: A zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the 2-hydroxy group to the 1-amino group of tetracycline. It is the major microspecies at pH 7.3 (according to Marvin v 6.2.0.).
label: tetracycline zwitterion

definition: Any antifungal agent used to prevent or treat fungal infections in humans or animals.
label: antifungal drug

definition: A product in capsule, tablet or liquid form that provide essential nutrients, such as a vitamin, an essential mineral, a protein, an herb, or similar nutritional substance.
label: nutraceutical

definition: An  organic molecule that is electrically neutral carrying a positive and a negative charge in one of its major canonical descriptions. In most dipolar compounds the charges are delocalized; however the term is also applied to species where this is not the case.
label: dipolar compound

definition: A cyclodepsipeptide that is N-(3-hydroxypicolinoyl)-L-threonyl-D-α-aminobutyryl-L-prolyl-N-methyl-L-phenylalanyl-4-oxo-L-pipecoloyl-L-2-phenylglycine in which the carboxy group of the 2-phenylglycine moiety has undergone formal intramolecular condensation with the hydroxy group of the N-(3-hydroxypicolinoyl)-L-threonyl to give the corresponding 19-membered ring lactone. It is one of the two major components of the antibacterial drug virginiamycin, produced by Streptomyces virginiae, S. loidensis, S. mitakaensis, S. pristina-spiralis, S. ostreogriseus, and others.
label: virginiamycin S1

definition: A substance that diminishes the rate of a chemical reaction.
label: inhibitor

definition: Any substance used in acriculture, horticulture, forestry, etc. for its fungicidal properties.
label: antifungal agrochemical

definition: Solvent that is capable of acting as a hydron (proton) acceptor.
label: protophilic solvent

definition: An agent that produces a soft formed stool, and relaxes and loosens the bowels, typically used over a protracted period, to relieve constipation. Compare with cathartic, which is a substance that accelerates defecation. A substances can be both a laxative and a cathartic.
label: laxative

definition: A gas in an atmosphere that absorbs and emits radiation within the thermal infrared range, so contributing to the 'greenhouse effect'.
label: greenhouse gas

definition: A salt is an assembly of cations and anions.
label: salt

definition: A drug used to produce muscle relaxation (excepting neuromuscular blocking agents). Its primary clinical and therapeutic use is the treatment of muscle spasm and immobility associated with strains, sprains, and injuries of the back and, to a lesser degree, injuries to the neck. Also used for the treatment of a variety of clinical conditions that have in common only the presence of skeletal muscle hyperactivity, for example, the muscle spasms that can occur in multiple sclerosis.
label: muscle relaxant

definition: The conjugate base of clavulanic acid.
label: clavulanate

definition: A mixture secreted by the hypopharyngeal gland of young worker bees (Apis mellifera) and fed as it is secreted to the queen bee and to larvae that are being raised as potential queen bees; it is not stored. Water makes up about two thirds of fresh royal jelly, with the remainder consisting mostly of proteins and sugars, followed by lipids (mostly free fatty acids containing short (8 to 10 carbon atom) chains with uncommon structures) and water-soluble vitamins.
label: royal jelly

definition: An erythromycin that consists of erythronolide A having 2,6-dideoxy-3-C-methyl-3-O-methyl-α-L-ribo-hexopyranosyl and 3,4,6-trideoxy-3-(dimethylamino)-β-D-xylo-hexopyranosyl residues attahced at positions 4 and 6 respectively.
label: erythromycin A

definition: A cyclic peptide antibiotic produced by the actinomycete Streptomyces puniceus, used in the treatment of tuberculosis.
label: viomycin

definition: A macromolecule formed by a living organism.
label: biomacromolecule

definition: A maltodextrin in which the α-(1→4)-linked <small>D</small>-glucose units form a linear chain, typically from 3 to 17 glucose units long. (Cf. amylose, in which the chain length ranges from around 300 to several thousand glucose units).
label: linear maltodextrin

definition: Any compound that is added to manufactured materials to inhibit, suppress, or delay the production of flames and so prevent the spread of fire.
label: flame retardant

definition: A carbohydrate derivative arising formally from the elimination of water from a glycosidic hydroxy group and an H atom bound to an oxygen, carbon, nitrogen or sulfur atom of a separate entity.
label: glycosyl compound

definition: Any compound that is able to prevent damage to the liver.
label: hepatoprotective agent

definition: Biologically active substance whose activity affects or plays a role in the functioning of the immune system.
label: immunomodulator

definition: An α-L-Fucp-(1→6)-D-Glcp in which the carbon bearing the anomeric hydroxy group has α configuration.
label: alpha-L-Fucp-(1->6)-alpha-D-Glcp

definition: An amino disaccharide consisting of an α-<small>D</small>-glucopyranose residue and a 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-<small>D</small>-glucopyranose residue joined in sequence by a (1→4) glycosidic bond.
label: alpha-D-Glcp-(1->4)-D-GlcpNAc

definition: O-phosphoviomycin protonated to pH 7.3.
label: O-phosphoviomycin(1+)

definition: A <small>D</small>-glucopyranose 1-phosphate in which the anomeric centre has α-configuration.
label: alpha-D-glucose 1-phosphate

definition: Any polyatomic entity that is an electrically neutral entity consisting of more than one atom.
label: molecule

definition: A simple monocarboxylic acid containing two carbons.
label: acetic acid

definition: An amino disaccharide that is α-<small>D</small>-glucopyranose in which the hydroxy group at position 3 has been converted into the corresponding 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-β-<small>D</small>-glucopyranosyl derivative.
label: beta-D-GlcpNAc-(1->3)-alpha-D-Glcp

definition: Antibiotic isolated from Streptomyces clavuligerus. It acts as a suicide inhibitor of bacterial β-lactamase enzymes.
label: clavulanic acid

definition: Any member of the class of organooxygen compounds that is a polyhydroxy-aldehyde or -ketone or a lactol resulting from their intramolecular condensation (monosaccharides); substances derived from these by reduction of the carbonyl group (alditols), by oxidation of one or more hydroxy groups to afford the corresponding aldehydes, ketones, or carboxylic acids, or by replacement of one or more hydroxy group(s) by a hydrogen atom; and polymeric products arising by intermolecular acetal formation between two or more such molecules (disaccharides, polysaccharides and oligosaccharides). Carbohydrates contain only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen atoms; prior to any oxidation or reduction, most have the empirical formula Cm(H2O)n. Compounds obtained from carbohydrates by substitution, etc., are known as carbohydrate derivatives and may contain other elements. Cyclitols are generally not regarded as carbohydrates.
label: carbohydrate

definition: Any oligosaccharide, polysaccharide or their derivatives consisting of monosaccharides or monosaccharide derivatives linked by glycosidic bonds. See also http://www.ontobee.org/ontology/GNO?iri=http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GNO_00000001.
label: glycan

definition: Aldehydic parent sugars (polyhydroxy aldehydes H[CH(OH)]nC(=O)H, n ≥ 2) and their intramolecular hemiacetals.
label: aldose

definition: A polar solvent that is capable of acting as a hydron (proton) donor.
label: protic solvent

definition: A mixture consisting of urea (typically 40-45%), ammonium nitrate (30-35%) and water (30-20%). It is used as a nitrogen fertilizer in agriculture.
label: urea ammonium nitrate

definition: A monoatomic or polyatomic species having one or more elementary charges of the electron.
label: anion

definition: A role played by the molecular entity or part thereof within a biological context.
label: biological role

definition: A depsipeptide in which the amino and hydroxy carboxylic acid residues are connected in a ring.
label: cyclodepsipeptide

definition: Any monosaccharide containing an alcoholic hydroxy group esterified with phosphoric acid.
label: phospho sugar

definition: A molecular entity consisting of two or more chemical elements.
label: heteroatomic molecular entity

definition: A compound in which a hydroxy group, ‒OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom.
label: alcohol

definition: An atom or small molecule with a positive charge that does not contain carbon in covalent linkage, with a valency of one.
label: monovalent inorganic cation

definition: Any amino-acid that is not naturally encoded in the genetic code of any organism.
label: non-proteinogenic amino acid

definition: A subclass of polyketides having an octahydrotetracene-2-carboxamide skeleton, substituted with many hydroxy and other groups.
label: tetracyclines

definition: A ketone containing a hydroxy group on the α-carbon relative to the C=O group.
label: alpha-hydroxy ketone

definition: A triamine that is the 1,5,10-triaza derivative of decane.
label: spermidine

definition: Any ether carrying a hydroxy group at unspecified position.
label: hydroxyether

definition: Any compound containing the carbonyl group, C=O. The term is commonly used in the restricted sense of aldehydes and ketones, although it actually includes carboxylic acids and derivatives.
label: carbonyl compound

definition: Any molecular entity consisting of more than one atom.
label: polyatomic entity

definition: A molecular entity containing one or more atoms from any of groups 1, 2, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, and 18 of the periodic table.
label: main group molecular entity

definition: An acene that consists of four ortho-fused benzene rings in a rectilinear arrangement.
label: tetracene

definition: A cyclically conjugated molecular entity with a stability (due to delocalization) significantly greater than that of a hypothetical localized structure (e.g. Kekulé structure) is said to possess aromatic character.
label: aromatic compound

definition: Derivatives of oxoacids RnE(=O)OH in which the hydroxy group is replaced by an amino group and the oxo group is replaced by =NR. In organic chemistry an unspecified amidine is commonly a carboxamidine.
label: amidine

definition: A peptide cation in which the peptide is cyclic.
label: cyclic peptide cation

definition: A tryptamine alkaloid that is N,N-dimethyltryptamine carrying an additional hydroxy substituent at position 4. A hallucinogenic alkaloid isolated in trace amounts from Psilocybe mushrooms (also known as Teonanácatl or "magic mushrooms").
label: psilocin

definition: Viomycin protonated to pH 7.3
label: viomycin(3+)

definition: A heterodetic cyclic peptide is a peptide consisting only of amino-acid residues, but in which the linkages forming the ring are not solely peptide bonds; one or more is an isopeptide, disulfide, ester, or other bond.
label: heterodetic cyclic peptide

definition: A lactam in which the amide bond is contained within a four-membered ring, which includes the amide nitrogen and the carbonyl carbon.
label: beta-lactam

definition: An azole based on a five-membered heterocyclic aromatic skeleton containing one N and one O atom.
label: oxazole

definition: A compound formally derived from an oxoacid RkE(=O)l(OH)m (l > 0) and an alcohol, phenol, heteroarenol, or enol by linking with formal loss of water from an acidic hydroxy group of the former and a hydroxy group of the latter.
label: ester

definition: Any inhibitor that acts on uncoupling protein.
label: uncoupling protein inhibitor

definition: A heterocyclic compound formally derived from an arene by replacement of one or more methine (‒C=) and/or vinylene (‒CH=CH‒) groups by trivalent or divalent heteroatoms, respectively, in such a way as to maintain the continuous π-electron system characteristic of aromatic systems and a number of out-of-plane π-electrons corresponding to the Hückel rule (4n+2).
label: heteroarene

definition: Any substance which when absorbed into a living organism may modify one or more of its functions. The term is generally accepted for a substance taken for a therapeutic purpose, but is also commonly used for abused substances.
label: drug

definition: A carbon oxoacid acid carrying at least one ‒C(=O)OH group and having the structure RC(=O)OH, where R is any any monovalent functional group. Carboxylic acids are the most common type of organic acid.
label: carboxylic acid

definition: Any magnesium ion that is positively charged.
label: magnesium cation

definition: A polar amino acid zwitterion of <small>L</small>-ornithine.
label: L-ornithinium(1+)

definition: An antiviral agent that destroys or inhibits the replication of the human immunodeficiency virus.
label: anti-HIV agent

definition: Any substance which is added to food to preserve or enhance its flavour and/or appearance.
label: food additive

definition: Any organonitrogen compound containing a cyclic component with nitrogen and at least one other element as ring member atoms.
label: organonitrogen heterocyclic compound

definition: Amide derived from two or more amino carboxylic acid molecules (the same or different) by formation of a covalent bond from the carbonyl carbon of one to the nitrogen atom of another with formal loss of water. The term is usually applied to structures formed from α-amino acids, but it includes those derived from any amino carboxylic acid. X = OH, OR, NH2, NHR, etc.
label: peptide

definition: A purine ribonucleotide where the purine is guanine.
label: guanyl ribonucleotide

definition: A divalent metal cation in which the metal is manganese.
label: manganese(2+)

definition: An addition compound that contains water in weak chemical combination with another compound.
label: hydrate

definition: An α-D-Glcp-(1→4)-D-Galp in which the carbon bearing the anomeric hydroxy group has β configuration.
label: alpha-D-Glcp-(1->4)-beta-D-Galp

definition: A drug which lowers the blood glucose level.
label: hypoglycemic agent

definition: A xenobiotic (Greek, xenos "foreign"; bios "life") is a compound that is foreign to a living organism. Principal xenobiotics include: drugs, carcinogens and various compounds that have been introduced into the environment by artificial means.
label: xenobiotic

definition: Any substance or mixture of substances that, in solution (typically aqueous), resists change in pH upon addition of small amounts of acid or base.
label: buffer

definition: Compounds having the structure RC(=NR)NR<small><sub>2</sub></small>. The term is used as a suffix in systematic nomenclature to denote the ‒C(=NH)NH<small><sub>2</sub></small> group including its carbon atom.
label: carboxamidine

definition: Any derivative of an amino acid resulting from reaction at an amino group, carboxy group, side-chain functional group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen by a heteroatom. The definition normally excludes peptides containing amino acid residues.
label: amino-acid derivative

definition: 2-Deoxy-<small>D</small>-streptamine glycosylated at the 4-oxygen with a 6-amino-α-<small>D</small>-glucosaminyl group.
label: neamine

definition: A glucan composed of unbranched chains of <small>D</small>-glucopyranose residues in α(1→4) glycosidic linkage. The number of repeated glucose subunits (n) is usually in the range of 300 to 3000, but can be many thousands. One of the two components of starch (the other, 70-80%, being amylopectin). Cf. linear maltodextrin, in which the chain length is typically between 3 and 17 glucose units.
label: amylose

definition: A carboxamide resulting from the formal condensation of a carboxylic acid with the amino group of an amino acid.
label: N-acyl-amino acid

definition: An optically active form of ornithine having <small>L</small>-configuration.
label: L-ornithine

definition: A monosaccharide derivative that is formally obtained from a pentose.
label: pentose derivative

definition: A mononuclear parent hydride consisting of covalently bonded hydrogen and chlorine atoms.
label: hydrogen chloride

definition: Tetracycline in which the hydroxy group at position 5 and the methyl group at position 6 are replaced by hydrogen, and with a dimethylamino substituent and an (N-tert-butylglycyl)amino substituent at positions 7 and 9, respectively. A glycylcycline antibiotic, it has activity against a broad range of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including tetracycline-resistant organisms. It is used for the intravenous treatment of complicated skin and skin structure infections caused by susceptible organisms.
label: tigecycline

definition: An oxoacid containing a single carboxy group.
label: monocarboxylic acid

definition: Any compound that supports healthy aging, slows the biological aging process, or extends lifespan.
label: geroprotector

definition: Any substance introduced into a living organism with therapeutic or diagnostic purpose.
label: pharmaceutical

definition: A monoatomic entity is a molecular entity consisting of a single atom.
label: monoatomic entity

definition: A drug used for its actions on skeletal muscle.
label: neuromuscular agent

definition: A poly(ethylene glycol) that is octane-1,8-diol in which the carbon atoms at positions 3 and 6 have been replaced by oxygen atoms.
label: triethylene glycol

definition: Any of the 23 α-amino acids that are precursors to proteins, and are incorporated into proteins during translation. The group includes the 20 amino acids encoded by the nuclear genes of eukaryotes together with selenocysteine, pyrrolysine, and N-formylmethionine. Apart from glycine, which is non-chiral, all have L configuration.
label: proteinogenic amino acid

definition: Any lactone in which the cyclic carboxylic ester group forms a part of a cyclic macromolecule.
label: macrocyclic lactone

definition: An amino disaccharide consisting of α-<small>D</small>-glucopyranose and 2-acetamido-2-deoxyalpha-<small>D</small>-galactopyranose residues joined in sequence by a (1→3) glycosidic bond.
label: alpha-D-Glcp-(1->3)-alpha-D-GalpNAc

definition: Any nutrient required in small quantities by organisms throughout their life in order to orchestrate a range of physiological functions.
label: micronutrient

definition: A class of imidazopyrimidines that consists of purine and its substituted derivatives.
label: purines

definition: A halide anion formed when chlorine picks up an electron to form an an anion.
label: chloride

definition: An organophosphorus compound is formally a compound containing at least one carbon-phosphorus bond, but the term is often extended to include esters and thioesters.
label: organophosphorus compound

definition: Any polyamine that contains two amino groups.
label: diamine

definition: A derivative of ammonium, NH<small><sub>4</sub></small><small><sup>+</small></sup>, in which one (or more) of the hydrogens bonded to the nitrogen have been replaced with univalent organyl groups. The substituting carbon of the organyl group must not itself be directly attached to a heteroatom (thereby excluding protonated amides, hemiaminals, etc).
label: ammonium ion derivative

definition: An aldohexose used as a source of energy and metabolic intermediate.
label: glucose

definition: Strictly, a substance intended to kill pests. In common usage, any substance used for controlling, preventing, or destroying animal, microbiological or plant pests.
label: pesticide

definition: An organophosphate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate and phosphonate OH groups of guanosine 5'-[β,γ-imido]triphosphate.
label: guanosine 5'-[beta,gamma-imido]triphosphate(4-)

definition: A cyclic compound having as ring members atoms of at least two different elements.
label: heterocyclic compound

definition: Any cyclitol having one or more alcoholic hydroxy groups replaced by substituted or unsubstituted amino groups.
label: amino cyclitol

definition: Any purine having at least one amino substituent.
label: aminopurine

definition: Any derivative of a proteinogenic amino acid resulting from reaction at an amino group, carboxy group, or a side-chain functional group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen by a heteroatom.
label: proteinogenic amino acid derivative

definition: A chemically diverse class of peptides that exhibit antimicrobial properties.
label: peptide antibiotic

definition: An α-hydroxy ketone in which the carbonyl group and the hydroxy group are linked by a carbon bearing two organyl groups.
label: tertiary alpha-hydroxy ketone

definition: Poisonous substance produced by a biological organism such as a microbe, animal or plant.
label: toxin

definition: A  purine ribonucleoside 5'-diphosphate resulting from the formal condensation of the hydroxy group at the 5' position of guanosine with pyrophosphoric acid.
label: GDP

definition: A chemical compound, or part thereof, which causes the onset of an allergic reaction by interacting with any of the molecular pathways involved in an allergy.
label: allergen

definition: Any cyclic carboxylic ester containing a 1-oxacycloalkan-2-one structure, or an analogue having unsaturation or heteroatoms replacing one or more carbon atoms of the ring.
label: lactone

definition: Any eukaryotic metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in plants, the kingdom that include flowering plants, conifers and other gymnosperms.
label: plant metabolite

definition: A diol in which the two hydroxy groups are on different carbon atoms, usually but not necessarily adjacent.
label: glycol

definition: A traditional grouping of drugs said to have a soothing or calming effect on mood, thought or behaviour.
label: tranquilizing drug

definition: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing two hydrogen atoms by organyl groups.
label: secondary amino compound

definition: A carbohydrate derivative that is formally obtained from a monosaccharide.
label: monosaccharide derivative

definition: An O-acyl carbohydrate that is α-D-glucose bearing a trans-4-coumaroyl substituent at position 6.
label: 6-O-(trans-4-coumaroyl)-alpha-D-glucopyranose

definition: Any minor or unwanted substance introduced into the environment that can have undesired effects.
label: environmental contaminant

definition: An inorganic chloride salt having sodium(1+) as the counterion.
label: sodium chloride

definition: A derivative of viomycin having a phospho group attached to the side-chain OH group of one of the serine residues.
label: O-phosphoviomycin

definition: A hydroxyether compound containing more than one ether group.
label: hydroxypolyether

definition: Any organooxygen compound that is a polyhydroxy-aldehyde or -ketone, or a compound derived from one. Carbohydrates contain only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen and usually have an empirical formula Cm(H2O)n; carbohydrate derivatives may contain other elements by substitution or condensation.
label: carbohydrates and carbohydrate derivatives

definition: An aminoglycoside that is 4α,6α-diaminocyclohexane-1β,2α,3β-triol in which the pro-R hydroxy group has been converted into its 2-acetamido-α-D-glucoside derivative.
label: 2'-N-acetylparomamine

definition: A dipeptide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of <small>L</small>-ornithine with the amino group of <small>D</small>-glutamic acid. It is a constituent of bacterial peptidoglycan type A4β.
label: L-Orn-D-Glu

definition: An organic anion that is the conjugate base of tetracycline zwitterion obtained by deprotonation of the two enolic hydroxy groups and protonation of the tertiary amino group.
label: tetracycline(1-)

definition: One of various classes of drugs with different action mechanisms used to treat or ameliorate peptic ulcer or irritation of the gastrointestinal tract.
label: anti-ulcer drug

definition: A loosely defined grouping of drugs that have effects on psychological function.
label: psychotropic drug

definition: A glucan derivative that is (1→4)-α-<small>D</small>-glucan in which the 6-position of the repeating unit has been phosphorylated.
label: (1->4)-6-phospho-alpha-D-glucan

definition: An α-D-Galp-(1→2)-D-Glcp in which the carbon bearing the anomeric hydroxy group has α configuration.
label: alpha-D-Galp-(1->2)-alpha-D-Glcp

definition: Hydroxides are chemical compounds containing a hydroxy group or salts containing hydroxide (OH<small><sup>−</small></sup>).
label: hydroxides

definition: A glycosylglucose that is α-<small>D</small>-glucopyranose in which the hydroxy group at position 4 has been glycosylated by an α-<small>L</small>-fucopyranosyl group.
label: alpha-L-Fucp-(1->4)-alpha-D-Glcp

definition: An organooxygen compound with formula ROR, where R is not hydrogen.
label: ether

definition: A guanosine 5'-phosphate that is the N2,N2,N7-trimethyl derivative of guanosine 5'-triphosphate.
label: N(2),N(2),N(7)-trimethylguanosine 5'-triphosphate(1+)

definition: Cyclic amides of amino carboxylic acids, having a 1-azacycloalkan-2-one structure, or analogues having unsaturation or heteroatoms replacing one or more carbon atoms of the ring.
label: lactam

definition: A Daphnia metabolite produced by the species Daphnia magna.
label: Daphnia magna metabolite

definition: Any compound used for the treatment of eye conditions or eye diseases.
label: ophthalmology drug

definition: An antiviral agent that destroys or inhibits the replication of the hepatitis B virus.
label: anti-HBV agent

definition: Any drug used in the treatment of acute or chronic vascular hypertension regardless of pharmacological mechanism.
label: antihypertensive agent

definition: A ribosyl or deoxyribosyl derivative of a pyrimidine or purine base in which C-5 of the ribose ring is mono-, di-, tri- or tetra-phosphorylated.
label: nucleoside 5'-phosphate

definition: A compound that, on administration, must undergo chemical conversion by metabolic processes before becoming the pharmacologically active drug for which it is a prodrug.
label: prodrug

definition: An azole in which the five-membered heterocyclic aromatic skeleton contains three N atoms and two C atoms.
label: triazoles

definition: Any prokaryotic metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in bacteria.
label: bacterial metabolite

definition: Any fungal metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae ).
label: Saccharomyces cerevisiae metabolite

definition: A tertiary alcohol is a compound in which a hydroxy group, ‒OH, is attached to a saturated carbon atom which has three other carbon atoms attached to it.
label: tertiary alcohol

definition: A drug used in treating and healing of wounds.
label: vulnerary

definition: A compound which contains oxygen, at least one other element, and at least one hydrogen bound to oxygen, and which produces a conjugate base by loss of positive hydrogen ion(s) (hydrons).
label: oxoacid

definition: A polyol consisting of a cycloalkane containing at least three hydroxy groups, each attached to a different ring carbon atom.
label: cyclitol

definition: An ammonium ion that is the trication of spermidine, formed by protonation at all three nitrogens.
label: spermidine(3+)

definition: A glycosyl compound resulting from the attachment of a glycosyl group to a non-acyl group RO‒, RS‒, RSe‒, etc. The bond between the glycosyl group and the non-acyl group is called a glycosidic bond. By extension, the terms N-glycosides and C-glycosides are used as class names for glycosylamines and for compounds having a glycosyl group attached to a hydrocarbyl group respectively. These terms are misnomers and should not be used. The preferred terms are glycosylamines and C-glycosyl compounds, respectively.
label: glycoside

definition: An enzyme inhibitor that interferes with one or more steps in a metabolic pathway.
label: pathway inhibitor

definition: A glycophytoceramide having an α-<small>D</small>-glucopyranosyl residue at the O-1 position and an icosa-11,14-dienoyl group attached to the nitrogen.
label: 1-O-(alpha-D-glucopyranosyl)-N-icosa-11,14-dienoylphytosphingosine

definition: Any aminopurine having the amino substituent at the 2-position.
label: 2-aminopurines

definition: <small>D</small>-Glucopyranose having α-configuration at the anomeric centre.
label: alpha-D-glucose

definition: An oxygen hydride consisting of an oxygen atom that is covalently bonded to two hydrogen atoms
label: water

definition: A <small>D</small>-glucose 1,6-bisphosphate in which both phosphate groups are monophosphates.
label: alpha-D-glucose 1,6-bisphosphate

definition: A broad-spectrum polyketide antibiotic produced by the Streptomyces genus of actinobacteria.
label: tetracycline

definition: Anxiolytic drugs are agents that alleviate anxiety, tension, and anxiety disorders, promote sedation, and have a calming effect without affecting clarity of consciousness or neurologic conditions.
label: anxiolytic drug

definition: A macrolide that is (together with pristinamycin IA) a component of pristinamycin, an oral streptogramin antibiotic produced by Streptomyces pristinaespiralis. Pristinamycin exhibits bactericidal activity against Gram positive organisms including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
label: pristinamycin IIA

definition: A cyclic compound having as ring members atoms of carbon and at least of one other element.
label: organic heterocyclic compound

definition: Any heteroorganic entity containing at least one carbon-nitrogen bond.
label: organonitrogen compound

definition: Any animal metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in mammals.
label: mammalian metabolite

definition: A compound which increases either the number of red cells or the amount of haemoglobin in the blood.
label: anti-anaemic agent

definition: A molecular entity all atoms of which have the same atomic number.
label: elemental molecular entity

definition: A main group molecular entity that contains one or more atoms of a p-block element.
label: p-block molecular entity

definition: A glycosyl galactose consisting of an α-<small>D</small>-glucopyranose residue and a β-<small>D</small>-galactofuranose residue joined in sequence by a (1→2) glycosidic bond.
label: alpha-D-Glcp-(1->2)-beta-D-Galf

definition: An amino disaccharide consisting of an α-<small>D</small>-glucopyranose residue and a 2-acetamido-2-deoxy-α-<small>D</small>-allopyranose residue joined in sequence by a (1→4) glycosidic bond.
label: alpha-D-Glcp-(1->4)-alpha-D-AllpNAc

definition: Any eukaryotic metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in fungi, the kingdom that includes microorganisms such as the yeasts and moulds.
label: fungal metabolite

definition: A carboxamide derived from a monocarboxylic acid.
label: monocarboxylic acid amide

definition: A myricetin O-glucoside that is myricetin with a α-D-glucosyl residue attached at position 4'.
label: myricetin 4'-O-alpha-D-glucopyranoside

definition: Any conazole antifungal agent that has been used for the treatment of fungal infections in animals or humans.
label: conazole antifungal drug

definition: A drug used to treat or prevent infections caused by Mycobacteria, a genus of actinobacteria. Aerobic and nonmotile, members of the genus include the pathogens responsible for causing tuberculosis and leprosy.
label: antimycobacterial drug

definition: Any organooxygen compound derived from a carbohydrate by replacement of one or more hydroxy group(s) by an amino group, a thiol group or similar heteroatomic groups. The term also includes derivatives of these compounds.
label: carbohydrate derivative

definition: A difluorobenzene carrying fluoro groups at positions 1 and 3.
label: 1,3-difluorobenzene

definition: A biological role relating to the normal mechanisms and their interactions within a living system.
label: physiological role

definition: A glucopyranose having <small>D</small>-configuration.
label: D-glucopyranose

definition: Any metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in prokaryotes, the taxon that include members of domains such as the bacteria and archaea.
label: prokaryotic metabolite

definition: A biological role played by the molecular entity or part thereof within a biochemical context.
label: biochemical role

definition: Any compound that induces the process of autophagy (the self-digestion of one or more components of a cell through the action of enzymes originating within the same cell).
label: autophagy inducer

definition: Any azaalkane in which two or more carbons in the chain are replaced by nitrogen.
label: polyazaalkane

definition: Any of a group of aminoglycoside antibiotics produced by fermentation of some Micromonospora spp.
label: gentamycin

definition: A metal cation with a valence of two.
label: divalent metal cation

definition: The most important reserve polysaccharide found in plants. It is a glucan consisting of amylose and amylopectin.
label: starch

definition: A cyclic compound having as ring members atoms of the same element only.
label: homocyclic compound

definition: Natural and synthetic compounds containing alternating carbonyl and methylene groups ('β-polyketones'), biogenetically derived from repeated condensation of acetyl coenzyme A (via malonyl coenzyme A), and usually the compounds derived from them by further condensations, etc. Considered by many to be synonymous with the less frequently used terms acetogenins and ketides.
label: polyketide

definition: An amino acid derivative resulting from reaction of methionine at the amino group or the carboxy group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen of methionine  by a heteroatom. The definition normally excludes peptides containing methionine residues.
label: methionine derivative

definition: Any drug which can be used to prevent or alleviate glaucoma, a disease in which the optic nerve is damaged, resulting in progressive, irreversible loss of vision. It is often, though not always, associated with increased pressure of the fluid in the eye.
label: antiglaucoma drug

definition: An agent that suppresses cough. Antitussives have a central or a peripheral action on the cough reflex, or a combination of both. Compare with expectorants, which are considered to increase the volume of secretions in the respiratory tract, so facilitating their removal by ciliary action and coughing, and mucolytics, which decrease the viscosity of mucus, facilitating its removal by ciliary action and expectoration.
label: antitussive

definition: Any compound that has anti-asthmatic effects.
label: anti-asthmatic agent

definition: Any p-block molecular entity containing a chalcogen.
label: chalcogen molecular entity

definition: An alkane-α,ω-diammonium(2+) that is the dication of putrescine (1,4-butanediamine) arising from protonation of both primary amino groups; major species at pH 7.3.
label: 1,4-butanediammonium

definition: A polycyclic compound in which at least one of the rings contains at least one non-carbon atom.
label: heteropolycyclic compound

definition: An antiprotozoal drug used to treat or prevent infections caused by protozoan parasites that belong to the genus Leishmania.
label: antileishmanial agent

definition: Pentacation of gentamycin C<small><sub>1a</sub></small>.
label: gentamycin C1a(5+)

definition: Any ether that contains more than one ether linkage.
label: polyether

definition: An α-amino acid that is pentanoic acid bearing two amino substituents at positions 2 and 5.
label: ornithine

definition: An organic cation obtained by protonation of the secondary amino groups of spectinomycin.
label: spectinomycin(2+)

definition: A hemiacetal  having the structure R<small><sub>2</sub></small>C(OH)OR (R ≠ H), derived from a ketone by formal addition of an alcohol to the carbonyl group. The term 'cyclic hemiketals', once abandoned by IUPAC, has been reinstated as a subclass of hemiacetals.
label: cyclic hemiketal

definition: Any compound containing an indole skeleton.
label: indoles

definition: Any antibiotic antifungal agent that has been used as a fungicide.
label: antibiotic fungicide

definition: A molecular entity that can transfer ("donate") an electron, a pair of electrons, an atom or a group to another molecular entity.
label: donor

definition: Any organic heterocyclic compound containing at least one ring oxygen atom.
label: oxacycle

definition: Any organic ion with a net positive charge.
label: organic cation

definition: Any compound that inhibits one or more steps in the pathway leading to the synthesis of ergosterol.
label: ergosterol biosynthesis inhibitor

definition: The biological role played by a material entity when bound by a receptor of the adaptive immune system. Specific site on an antigen to which an antibody binds.
label: epitope

definition: Any organic amino compound that contains two or more amino groups.
label: polyamine

definition: Any zinc ion that is positively charged.
label: zinc cation

definition: A  nucleotide having adenine as the base.
label: adenyl nucleotide

config.description: A structured classification of molecular entities of biological interest focusing on 'small' chemical compounds.
config.title: Chemical Entities of Biological Interest

definition: A nucleoside triphosphate analogue that is GTP in which the oxygen atom bridging the β- to the γ- phosphate is replaced by a nitrogen atom A non-hydrolyzable analog of GTP, it binds tightly to G-protein in the presence of Mg<small><sup>2+</small></sup>.
label: guanosine 5'-[beta,gamma-imido]triphosphate

definition: A monosaccharide derivative that is (2R,3R,4R,5S)-2-(hydroxymethyl)piperidine-3,4,5-triol having an α-D-glucosyl residue attached at position 4.
label: 4-O-alpha-D-glucopyranosylmoranoline

definition: Any α-amino acid having <small>L</small>-configuration at the α-carbon.
label: L-alpha-amino acid

definition: A tetracyclic antibacterial agent derived from neomycin, being a glycoside ester of neamine and neobiosamine B.
label: framycetin

definition: Any <small>L</small>-α-amino acid which is not a member of the group of 23 proteinogenic amino acids.
label: non-proteinogenic L-alpha-amino acid

definition: An amide is a derivative of an oxoacid RkE(=O)l(OH)m (l ≠ 0) in which an acidic hydroxy group has been replaced by an amino or substituted amino group.
label: amide

definition: Trianion of GTP arising from deprotonation of three of the four phosphate OH groups.
label: GTP(3-)

definition: A derivative of an oxoacid RkE(=O)l(OH)m (l ≠ 0) in which an acidic hydroxy group has been replaced by an amino or substituted amino group.
label: primary amide

definition: An EC 3.5.* (hydrolases acting on non-peptide C-N bonds) inhibitor that interferes with the action of any non-peptide cyclic amide C-N hydrolase (EC 3.5.2.*).
label: EC 3.5.2.* (non-peptide cyclic amide C-N hydrolase) inhibitor

definition: A bicyclic compound in which at least one of the rings contains at least one skeletal heteroatom.
label: heterobicyclic compound

definition: A d-block molecular entity is a molecular entity containing one or more atoms of a d-block element.
label: d-block molecular entity

definition: Any organic molecule that consists of atoms connected in the form of a ring.
label: organic cyclic compound

definition: Any mammalian metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in a mouse (Mus musculus).
label: mouse metabolite

definition: A polysaccharide composed of glucose residues.
label: glucan

definition: A natural or synthetic compound having a sequence of amino and hydroxy carboxylic acid residues (usually α-amino and α-hydroxy acids), commonly but not necessarily regularly alternating.
label: depsipeptide

definition: A compound having a nitro group, ‒NO2 (free valence on nitrogen), which may be attached to carbon, nitrogen (as in nitramines), or oxygen (as in nitrates), among other elements (in the absence of specification, C-nitro compounds are usually implied).
label: nitro compound

definition: Any nucleotide that has a purine nucleobase.
label: purine nucleotide

definition: A homocyclic compound in which all of the ring members are carbon atoms.
label: carbocyclic compound

definition: An organosulfur compound is a compound containing at least one carbon-sulfur bond.
label: organosulfur compound

definition: A drug used to prevent seizures or reduce their severity.
label: anticonvulsant

definition: Tryptamine and its substitution derivatives.
label: tryptamines

definition: Cyclic hemiacetals formed by intramolecular addition of a hydroxy group to an aldehydic or ketonic carbonyl group. They are thus 1-oxacycloalkan-2-ols or unsaturated analogues.
label: lactol

definition: A clathrate compound that is an ice-like solid that consists of methane which is trapped within the crystal structure of water. It has formula CH<small><sub>4</sub></small>·5.75H<small><sub>2</sub></small>O or 4CH<small><sub>4</sub></small>·23H<small><sub>2</sub></small>O.
label: methane clathrate

definition: A glycosylgalactose consisting of an α-<small>D</small>-glucopyranose residue and a <small>D</small>-galactofuranose residue joined in sequence by a (1→2) glycosidic bond
label: alpha-D-Glcp-(1->2)-D-Galf

definition: An aminoglycoside that is 4α,6α-diaminocyclohexane-1β,2α,3β-triol in which the pro-R hydroxy group has been converted into its 2-amino-α-D-glucoside derivative.
label: paromamine

definition: A purine riboncleotide where adenine is the purine.
label: adenyl ribonucleotide

definition: Any compound that has anti-inflammatory effects.
label: anti-inflammatory agent

definition: Any compound that can be used for the treatment of neurodegenerative disorders.
label: neuroprotective agent

definition: A substance (or active part thereof) that kills or slows the growth of bacteria.
label: antibacterial agent

definition: An organochalcogen compound is a compound containing at least one carbon-chalcogen bond.
label: organochalcogen compound

definition: A drug used to treat or prevent skin disorders or for the routine care of skin.
label: dermatologic drug

definition: A glycosylglucose consisting of β-<small>L</small>-fucopyranose and α-<small>D</small>-glucopyranose residues joined in sequence by a (1→4) glycosidic bond.
label: beta-L-Fucp-(1->4)-alpha-D-Glcp

definition: A glycosylglucose consisting of a β-<small>L</small>-fucosyl residue and an α-<small>D</small>-glucopyranose residue joined in sequence by a (1→6) glycosidic bond.
label: beta-L-Fucp-(1->6)-alpha-D-Glcp

definition: A substance that dissolves other substances (solutes) to form a solution without any change in their chemical composition.
label: solvent

definition: A role played by the molecular entity or part thereof which causes the development of a pathological process.
label: aetiopathogenetic role

definition: A molecular entity containing one or more atoms of an alkali metal.
label: alkali metal molecular entity

definition: A carboxylic acid containing one or more amino groups.
label: amino acid

definition: A neutral compound having formal unit electrical charges of opposite sign on non-adjacent atoms. Sometimes referred to as inner salts, dipolar ions (a misnomer).
label: zwitterion

definition: An organic molecule or ion (usually a metal ion) that is required by an enzyme for its activity. It may be attached either loosely (coenzyme) or tightly (prosthetic group).
label: cofactor

definition: A p-block molecular entity containing any pnictogen.
label: pnictogen molecular entity

definition: A compound, usually an anti-bacterial agent or a toxin, which inhibits the synthesis of a protein.
label: protein synthesis inhibitor

definition: A compound that has a structure that is related to miconazole, contains an azole (imidazole or triazole) moiety, and has significant systemic antifungal properties.  They inhibit cytochrome P450-dependent enzymes (particularly C14-demethylase) involved in the biosynthesis of ergosterol, which is required for fungal cell membrane structure and function.
label: conazole antifungal agent

definition: A 1,2-glycol compound produced via reaction of ethylene oxide with water.
label: ethylene glycol

definition: Any compound that has a nucleobase as a part.
label: nucleobase-containing molecular entity

definition: An agent which overcomes insulin resistance by activation of the peroxisome proliferator activated receptor gamma (PPAR-gamma).
label: insulin-sensitizing drug

definition: An α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid amide of general formula R<small><sup>1</small></sup>R<small><sup>2</small></sup>C=CR<small><sup>3</small></sup>‒C(=O)NR<small><sup>4</small></sup>R<small><sup>5</small></sup> in which the amide C=O function is conjugated to a C=C double bond at the α,β position.
label: enamide

definition: An agent that suppresses immune function by one of several mechanisms of action. Classical cytotoxic immunosuppressants act by inhibiting DNA synthesis. Others may act through activation of T-cells or by inhibiting the activation of helper cells. In addition, an immunosuppressive agent is a role played by a compound which is exhibited by a capability to diminish the extent and/or voracity of an immune response.
label: immunosuppressive agent

definition: A tryptamine alkaloid that is N,N-dimethyltryptamine carrying an additional phosphoryloxy substituent at position 4. The major hallucinogenic alkaloid isolated from Psilocybe mushrooms (also known as Teonanácatl or "magic mushrooms").
label: psilocybin

definition: Any phospho sugar that is the phosphate derivative of pentose.
label: pentose phosphate

definition: Drugs capable of inducing illusions, hallucinations, delusions, paranoid ideations and other alterations of mood and thinking.
label: hallucinogen

definition: Substance intended to kill parasitic worms (helminths).
label: anthelminthic drug

definition: Any  α-amino acid which is not a member of the group of 23 proteinogenic amino acids.
label: non-proteinogenic alpha-amino acid

definition: A drug used in the treatment of malaria. Antimalarials are usually classified on the basis of their action against Plasmodia at different stages in their life cycle in the human.
label: antimalarial

definition: The aminoglycoside sulfate salt that is the sulfate salt of neomycin B; a component of neomycin sulfate.
label: neomycin B sulfate

definition: A hexose that has <small>D</small>-configuration at position 5.
label: D-hexose

definition: A substance that kills or slows the growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and is used in the treatment of tuberculosis.
label: antitubercular agent

definition: An amino acid in which the amino group is located on the carbon atom at the position α to the carboxy group.
label: alpha-amino acid

definition: Any benzenoid aromatic compound consisting of the benzene skeleton and its substituted derivatives.
label: benzenes

definition: A compound that contains two or more hydroxy groups.
label: polyol

definition: A carboxamide resulting from the formal condensation of a carboxylic acid with a secondary amine; formula RC(=O)NHR<small><sup>1</small></sup>R<small><sup>2</small></sup>.
label: tertiary carboxamide

definition: A glucose with <small>D</small>-configuration.
label: D-glucose

definition: A drug used to treat psoriasis.
label: antipsoriatic

definition: An aminoglycoside antibiotic that is gentamycin C1a in which the hydrogen of the amino group at position 1 is substituted by an ethyl group. It is a fourth generation semisynthetic aminoglycoside that has antimicrobial activity against both gram-positive and gram-negative bacterial infections and also effective against aminoglycoside resistant strains.
label: etimicin

definition: A primary diamine that is ethane or a higher alkane in which a hydrogen of each of the terminal methyl groups has been replaced by an amino group. H<small><sub>2</sub></small>NCH<small><sub>2</sub></small>(CH<small><sub>2</sub></small>)<small><sub>n</sub></small>CH<small><sub>2</sub></small>NH<small><sub>2</sub></small>, where n = 0, 1, 2, etc.
label: alkane-alpha,omega-diamine

definition: An s-block molecular entity is a molecular entity containing one or more atoms of an s-block element.
label: s-block molecular entity

definition: A substance used in the prophylaxis or therapy of infectious diseases.
label: antiinfective agent

definition: A 3-amino-3-deoxy-<small>D</small>-glucopyranose that has α-configuration at the anomeric position.
label: alpha-D-kanosamine

definition: A solvent that is composed of polar molecules. Polar solvents can dissolve ionic compounds or ionisable covalent compounds.
label: polar solvent

definition: A compound containing at least one carbon-halogen bond (where X is a halogen atom).
label: organohalogen compound

definition: A glycol that is the (S)-enantiomer of 2-methylpentane-2,4-diol.
label: (4S)-2-methylpentane-2,4-diol

definition: Any  metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in eukaryotes, the taxon that include members of the fungi, plantae and animalia kingdoms.
label: eukaryotic metabolite

definition: A food additive that is used to change or otherwise control the acidity or alkalinity of foods. They may be acids, bases, neutralising agents or buffering agents.
label: food acidity regulator

definition: A member of the class of triazole that has significant antifungal properties.
label: triazole antifungal agent

definition: A chemical substance is a portion of matter of constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same type or of different types.
label: chemical substance

definition: Any p-block element belonging to the group 16 family of the periodic table.
label: chalcogen

definition: A cation formed by protonation of a peptide.
label: peptide cation

definition: An animal metabolite produced by arthropods such as crabs, lobsters, crayfish, shrimps and krill.
label: crustacean metabolite

definition: Any monocyclic heteroarene consisting of a five-membered ring containing nitrogen. Azoles can also contain one or more other non-carbon atoms, such as nitrogen, sulfur or oxygen.
label: azole

definition: An oxidoreductase inhibitor which interferes with the action of an oxidoreductase acting on hydrogen as donors (EC 1.14.*.*).
label: EC 1.14.* (oxidoreductase acting on paired donors, with incorporation or reduction of molecular oxygen) inhibitor

definition: A nucleobase-containing molecular entity that is a nucleoside in which one or more of the sugar hydroxy groups has been converted into a mono- or poly-phosphate. The term includes both nucleotides and non-nucleotide nucleoside phosphates.
label: nucleoside phosphate

definition: The conjugate base of N-formyl-L-methionine; major species at pH 7.3.
label: N-formyl-L-methioninate

definition: Any enzyme inhibitor that interferes with the action of a hydrolase (EC 3.*.*.*).
label: EC 3.* (hydrolase) inhibitor

definition: A drug used to relieve nasal congestion in the upper respiratory tract.
label: nasal decongestant

definition: Any protective agent counteracting or neutralizing the action of poisons.
label: antidote

definition: An amino cyclitol glycoside that is isolated from Streptomyces kasugaensis and exhibits antibiotic and fungicidal properties.
label: kasugamycin

definition: Any antiviral agent which inhibits the activity of coronaviruses.
label: anticoronaviral agent
